findings.message:
Do not roll stale RFC-850 dates into the next century

The candidate search chooses the nearest of current, previous, and next centuries. RFC 9110's rule only rolls the current-century interpretation back when it is more than 50 years in the future; it must not roll an already-past date forward. For example, around 2070 a valid `01-Jan-00` date is past and should clamp to the observation time, but this selects 2100 and can block the installation for decades.

src/github/rate-limit.ts:195-205

Preserve the full accepted timestamp range

`observedAt` is accepted as any nonnegative safe integer, but `Date` clips values above 8.64e15 ms to an invalid date. For such an otherwise accepted observation, `getUTCFullYear()` is NaN and a valid RFC-850 hint is classified as malformed, changing a primary hold into a missing deadline (or causing a secondary fallback). Resolve the year without this narrower `Date` range or explicitly handle it as unrepresentable.

src/github/rate-limit.ts:187-188

summary: RFC-850 resolution can create spurious future cooldowns and mishandles otherwise accepted safe timestamps.
